description: Source-backed HUX work-in-progress plan. Proposed and simulated work is separate from measured physical evidence. Null order quantities and costs mean unknown, not zero.

maintenance.sourceOfTruth: Repository documents and recorded physical evidence
instructions: Update the relevant source document and this plan together when a decision, order or measured result changes.
Record dates, exact parts, quantities and actual costs; unknown values remain null.
Move physical milestones to passed only with linked session records, logs and measured acceptance evidence.
Keep failed trials and superseded decisions in history. Simulation results never close hardware acceptance.

versions.name: V1-PROOF
versions.summary: The current HUX: a small, four-actuator wheeled robot to prove balance, manual driving and slow leg-height changes for strictly less than $1,000.

focus.title: Prepare the single-leg actuator bench
focus.summary: One Pololu 4752 motor and one Pololu 4035 driver are shipped; two ST3215 servos are paid and awaiting shipment in the latest vendor record. $143.12 is paid in total. These parts lock the one-leg/one-wheel bench baseline; the full robot still needs its second wheel motor and driver. No physical test has been completed.

nextActions.title: Receive and identify the ordered parts
nextActions.detail: Check the incoming Pololu motor/driver against the receipt and the two ST3215 servos against the requested 12 V variant. Pololu shipment email estimates 1 October; servo dispatch is unconfirmed. Record delivery, labels, dimensions and condition.

nextActions.title: Prepare the passive bench fixture
nextActions.detail: The Bambu X1C / PLA passive kit is drafted. Print and measure its fit coupon first; M4 clearances are provisional. Then mock up the 110 mm links and 40 mm pivot spacing by hand, using the 1:1 template as a reference. The supported powered fixture, lock, catch and actuator-specific fits still need detailing.

nextActions.title: Confirm controls and power interfaces
nextActions.detail: One DRV8874 is coming with the wheel motor. Confirm the Pico 2, IMU, half-duplex servo interface, encoder level conversion, harness and protected power rails. Record bench-supply ratings. The second wheel motor/driver remain unpurchased in the current records.

nextActions.title: Resolve power and return-energy protection
nextActions.detail: Prepare a fused harness and independent actuator-power cut. Verify supply behavior, current limits and a regeneration path before loaded lowering, backdriving or aggressive reversals.

nextActions.title: Open the first measured session
nextActions.detail: On arrival, identify the received hardware, then follow the staged bench sequence. Save wiring/firmware revision, measurements, photos, logs and failed trials in a copied session record.

milestones.title: Inventory and layout
milestones.summary: Paid receipts establish one wheel motor, one driver and two leg servos. Incoming actuator models are locked; received dimensions, electronics interfaces and second wheel channel remain open.
criteria: Record exact parts, variants, quantities, costs and reusable stock.
Quote missing items and retain reserves inside the strict cash cap.
Check mass allocations and the full wheel, motor, bearing, battery and cable envelopes.
Detail the pinned structure and a supported reduced-servo leg before final machining.

milestones.title: One-leg actuator exercise
milestones.summary: Prepare now; test one supported leg and lifted wheel after the parts and interfaces are identified. This can precede balance.
criteria: Complete the staged session with bounded commands, measured signs and disabled startup.
Record passive clearances, backlash and measured leg/wheel response.
Demonstrate independent power cut and implemented fault behavior in the fixture.
Use measured load, electrical and thermal results to inform the robot; a bench pass does not prove balance.

milestones.title: Supported wheels and pinned chassis
milestones.summary: Qualify the wheel channels and basic electronics before attempting free-standing balance.
criteria: Build supported axles, pinned neutral legs, rest skids and a catch fixture.
Verify motor/encoder polarity, current limits, low-voltage response and thermal behavior.
Test physical kill, watchdog, reset, stale commands and sensor faults with deliberate rearm.
Measure assembled mass, center of mass, timing and power behavior.

milestones.title: Pinned-leg balance and manual drive
milestones.summary: Prove two-wheel mobility with both legs mechanically pinned at neutral.
criteria: Hold balance for 60 seconds in at least 9 of 10 starts without support contact.
Complete logged 2 m forward/reverse runs, left/right arcs and both 360° in-place turns under the physical protocol.
Complete five combined sequences at bounded speed, on the required floors and voltages.
Keep failures and configuration hashes; simulated success does not close this gate.

milestones.title: Powered leg-height adjustment
milestones.summary: Add supported 3:1 reductions after pinned-leg balance; qualify each leg before synchronized movement.
criteria: Qualify 0.75 N·m mounted servo hold for 10 minutes and the separate 1.0 N·m short transient target.
Measure backlash, loaded clearance and pose-dependent pitch trim.
Complete ten low/high/low cycles with both wheels loaded, targeting at least 25 mm actual body-height change.
No support contact, overload or balance loss; use the measured qualified range.

milestones.title: Complete the physical proof
milestones.summary: Close the measured mobility, disturbance, fault, duty, mass and budget gates before expanding scope.
criteria: Qualify the specified 0.8 N·s longitudinal and 0.4 N·s lateral pulses, both signs and durations.
Qualify separate 3° slopes, 5 mm smooth bumps and 3 mm seam fixtures at 0.15 m/s.
Complete a 10-minute mixed session within measured electrical and thermal limits, with no resets.
Record final mass ≤3.0 kg and all-in new cash < $1,000.
Archive logs, videos and failure counts; replace model assumptions with measurements and rerun the matrix.

bench.title: Single-leg bench exercise
bench.summary: One restrained leg adjustment and one lifted driven wheel. Preparation plan dated 2026-09-29; no hardware has been tested. Start one actuator at a time. The full guide owns the wiring, power gates and detailed stop conditions.

geometry.label: Wheel
geometry.value: 100 mm nominal; lifted for first powered tests

stages.title: Identify received parts
stages.action: Record labels, quantities, pinouts, dimensions and condition.
stages.evidence: Confirmed inventory and a marked wiring diagram; template updated for actual parts.

stages.title: Power and readback
stages.action: Check disconnected rails and polarity, secure the bare servo, verify disabled startup and read feedback; read encoder counts with motor power off.
stages.evidence: Stable communications, expected counts per measured wheel revolution, and a verified independent power cut.

stages.title: Bare servo
stages.action: After verifying startup and target mapping, command ±5° at the servo output at no more than 5°/s with horn, belt and load removed.
stages.evidence: Correct direction with no startup jump, reset, unexpected current or tracking fault.

stages.title: Passive linkage
stages.action: Disconnect the drive and sweep the scrap linkage by hand through the 15–45° design range.
stages.evidence: No binding, cable contact or hardware collision; correct center spacing and functioning catch support.

stages.title: Small driven leg cycles
stages.action: Align at 30° with power off; remove the lock before arming. Begin 28–32° at 1°/s, holding 2 seconds at each end.
stages.evidence: Ten small cycles with independently measured angle, no jump or binding, and logged current, voltage and temperature.

stages.title: Wider unloaded travel
stages.action: After small-cycle success, try 25–35° and expand only within measured clearance and stop margins.
stages.evidence: Repeatable endpoints, measured vertical/fore-aft travel and approach-direction backlash; no stop strikes.

stages.title: Wheel alone
stages.action: Pin the leg, keep the wheel lifted and servo torque off. Verify sign, then try +10 rpm → 0 → −10 rpm, waiting for measured zero before reversal.
stages.evidence: Stable low-speed response with correct feedback sign; no reset or overvoltage. Record stiction before raising limits.

stages.title: Fault behavior
stages.action: Within the supported small-motion envelope, test deadman release, lost commands/feedback, reset, lost servo communication and physical kill.
stages.evidence: Faults latch, the catch contains torque loss, the cut works without software, and reconnection never rearms automatically.

stages.title: Combined unloaded motion
stages.action: After separate and fault tests, slowly sweep 28–32° while the lifted wheel turns at 10 rpm.
stages.evidence: Five repeatable cycles with no dropped commands, resets, wiring snags or rail violations.

stages.title: Measured loading
stages.action: Only after electrical and thermal gates, add a captured, measured load in steps with a known force direction and lever arm.
stages.evidence: Record deflection, backlash, temperature and rail behavior under load, including supported power loss. Later torque/duty qualification remains separate.

updates.title: Paid orders lock the actuator baseline
updates.summary: Reconciled Pololu and Waveshare receipts: one 4752 motor + one 4035 driver shipped ($88.34), and two ST3215 servos paid ($54.78), for $143.12 total including shipping/tax. The second wheel channel remains to buy. Added motor wiring and Pico control architecture; firmware and physical tests remain open.

updates.title: R01 passive print kit drafted
updates.summary: Eight STL part types and a Blender project are drafted for a Bambu X1C / PLA passive mockup using 110 mm link centers and 40 mm pivot spacing. M4 clearances are provisional: print and measure the fit coupon first. No physical print, fit, load test or bench milestone is complete. The ordered Pololu 4752 motors and ST3215 12 V servos remain awaiting arrival.

updates.title: Actuator orders and single-leg bench preparation
updates.summary: The user confirmed Pololu 4752 motors and ST3215 12 V servos ordered for V1-PROOF, awaiting arrival, and a bench supply available. Quantities, actual cost and supply ratings are pending. The supported one-leg exercise and session template are prepared; no hardware test is claimed.

updates.title: Mobility baseline and retained simulation failures
updates.summary: The pinned-leg numerical study passes 388 of 391 broad-matrix cases. The physical protocol covers both driving directions, turns, bounded pushes and shallow uneven fixtures. Three settling failures remain recorded; physical acceptance and powered-leg dynamics remain open.

updates.title: V1-PROOF becomes the current model
updates.summary: The stair-focused plan was parked. Active work moved to a smaller four-axis robot, pinned-leg balance first, with a strict sub-$1,000 budget and no stair requirement.

orders.deliveryNote: Shipped 28 September via UPS Ground. Shipment email estimates Thursday 1 October; not a live tracking check.

versions.name: V0-GENESIS
versions.summary: The original, ambitious stair-capable planning model. Parked on 2026-09-28; preserved as research and design history. Its old requirements and budgets do not govern V1-PROOF.

focus.title: Preserve the original planning history
focus.summary: V0-GENESIS is the user-facing name for the former STAIR-V1 planning archive. Existing stair-v1 file paths and historical labels remain provenance. Stair reach, single-support mechanics, actuator duty and full procurement release were unresolved when parked.

metrics.label: Original ambition
metrics.note: One wheeled leg at a time; historical target, not demonstrated capability.

metrics.label: Hardware release
metrics.note: Engineering and procurement gates remained open at the archive snapshot.

milestones.title: Research and architecture studies
milestones.summary: Preserved requirements, mass/geometry studies, actuator investigations and candidate layouts.

milestones.title: Stair engineering gates
milestones.summary: Reach, loaded contact mechanics, passive carrier design, actuator duty and procurement remained unresolved when work was parked.

updates.title: Stair planning parked
updates.summary: The user reset the project around an affordable proof robot. The existing stair planning model, documents, research and numerical work were preserved; reopening this architecture requires a later scope decision.

versions.name: Next version
versions.summary: The third HUX version follows V1-PROOF. Its name, requirements, budget and schedule are intentionally undecided.

focus.title: Let measured proof results define the next version
focus.summary: Carry forward measured actuator and sensor behavior, telemetry, fault handling and test evidence. Future full-size Hux has a stated RobStride direction, but no RobStride order or third-version hardware release is established.

nextActions.title: Close and archive the V1-PROOF evidence
nextActions.detail: Complete the physical acceptance gates and preserve logs, videos, failure counts and firmware/model revisions before selecting expanded requirements.

nextActions.title: Make an explicit next-version scope decision
nextActions.detail: Choose the third version’s name, requirements, architecture and budget from the proof’s measured results. V1 success does not promise a stair upgrade of the proof chassis.
